title: A bill to amend the Bill Emerson Good Samaritan Food Donation Act to improve the program, and for other purposes.
official_summary:
This bill expands liability protections for the donation of food and grocery products.

Specifically, the bill expands the liability protections to include donations of an apparently fit grocery product or apparently wholesome food

  • for which the recipient is charged a good Samaritan reduced price that is no greater than the cost of handling, administering, harvesting, processing, packaging, transporting, and distributing the food or product; or
  • that is donated directly to a needy individual at zero cost by a retail grocer, wholesaler, agricultural producer, agricultural processor, agricultural distributor, restaurant, caterer, school food authority, or institution of higher education.

summary.headline: This law widens legal protections for people and businesses that donate food and grocery products, including some donations sold at a low price.
summary.what_it_does: The law expands the liability protections under the Bill Emerson Good Samaritan Food Donation Act. Protection now covers donations of food or grocery products that appear fit or wholesome, even when the recipient pays a reduced "good Samaritan" price. That price must be no more than the cost of handling, processing, packaging, transporting, and distributing the item. Protection also covers food given directly to needy individuals at no cost.

who_it_affects.how: They gain liability protection when they donate food or grocery products, including at a reduced price that covers only their handling and distribution costs.
They gain liability protection when they donate food they grow, process, or distribute.
They gain liability protection when they donate food, including directly to needy individuals at no cost.

who_it_affects.group: School food authorities and institutions of higher education
who_it_affects.how: They gain liability protection when they donate food, including directly to needy individuals at no cost.
They may receive food or grocery products at no cost directly from the listed donors.
